findings.summary: Compiled embedding reduced NACA embedding time to 0.286 s; OCR now accounts for 86.5% of the 3.11 s diagnostic call.
observations: The current accepted configuration uses server concurrency eight, region window 64, dynamic pages and compiled BF16 embeddings in batches of sixteen. One warm-up, three ordinary calls and one separate instrumented full-PDF call all completed.
Median OCR time is 2.688 s and median embedding time is 0.286 s. Mean stage shares are 86.5% OCR, 9.2% embedding, 3.7% rendering and 0.6% chunking.

OCR-window mean GPU busy for GPUs 0–3 is [97.2, 96.8, 95.8, 95.3]%, with [6, 6, 6, 6] one-second samples. This short capture indicates sustained activity but does not establish peak compute or memory-bandwidth saturation.

All recognizers reached eight running requests and four waiting. Waiting requests appear in [17.1, 18.4, 22.4, 23.7]% of OCR-window scheduler snapshots. The previous sixteen-request trial already failed to improve performance.
All four bounded traces were captured; the complete instrumented output passed the frozen checks. Bounded traces cover only the first 32 engine iterations.
Attention now determines pooled p50 in the full five-PDF evaluation. A separate Attention profile checks that workload; the retained Census profile identifies a long single-region decode.
findings.next_step: Profile Attention, then test within-request GPU n-gram speculation while retaining the exact frozen OCR and chunk checks.
findings.optimization: Reduce serial decoder steps rather than increasing server admission again; inspect proposal acceptance, p50, p95 and throughput before accepting speculation.
